look_here_first: Start with the smooth-looking green compound leaves and upright woody shrub habit. Roemer's false indigo has pinnate leaves with relatively large mostly glabrous leaflets and terminal purple flower racemes that rise above the foliage.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — TPWD/TWDB environmental documentation records Texas amorpha near the proposed project area in Hays County. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Fabaceae specimen index includes Amorpha roemeriana and TxDOT element-occurrence records document a wild Travis County population. Bexar — TPWD annotated Bexar County rare-species lists and Government Canyon element-occurrence data document the species.

best_field_traits: leaflets relatively large and mostly glabrous compared with leadplant
terminal purple flower racemes or narrow clustered inflorescences
single-petaled Amorpha flowers with exserted stamens
limestone slopes, juniper-oak woodland, and rocky creek shelves
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with A. canescens, A. roemeriana is greener and less densely gray-hairy, with larger smoother-looking leaflets. Compared with A. fruticosa, it is generally a smaller limestone-hill-country shrub rather than a tall riparian thicket-former.
